newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil "regrets" January trade figure mix-up.
newsitem.headline: Brazil "regrets" January trade figure mix-up.

text.p: The Brazilian government regrets confusion caused by bureaucratic ineptness over January's trade figures, to which about $500 million in oil imports had to be added at the eleventh hour, a senior Finance Ministry official said.

Jose Roberto Mendonca de Barros, executive secretary of the Finance Ministry, said some low-level officials were aware early in January that state oil firm Petrobras was not registering its imports in the Siscomex computer system.
But he said they failed to "realize the implications for the trade balance" and for the markets.

Mendonca de Barros said Petrobras was slow to adapt to the new system of registering imports before they were offloaded in Brazilian ports, and that government bureaucracy also contributed to a delay in finding a solution.
Helio Mauro Franca, director of the foreign trade policy department in the Ministry of Industry and Commerce, said officials had been discussing the problem with Petrobras since early January.
Up to an hour before the trade data was due out Wednesday, government officials had been proudly announcing a trade surplus for the first time since May 1996.

But just before the release of the trade figures, the government noticed that the official oil imports were unusually low at about $61 million. Checks with Petrobras confirmed that the actual figure should have been almost ten times higher.
